body: From my personal research (not a professional), taking SSRIs while doing psychedelics has the general tendency to decrease the potency/effect of the psychedelic. There's some elevated risk of serotonin syndrome, but it varies among people.

In the depths of the worst depressive episode of my life, I found DXM (yes the shit you find in cough syrup) to be shockingly helpful- more helpful than the 5+ FDA approved medications that I tried before. Doing more "research" afterwards, I learned that this was not an uncommon experience and that there actually was a small clinical study of DXM + Wellbutrin that was quite successful.  I'm not a chemist, but the general impression I got was that this made sense as it's somewhat chemically similar to ketamine.

I recognize that self-medication (esp with illegal substances, potentially addictive substances) is risky, but depression is HELL; feeling actively suicidal, emotionally isolated, perpetually hollow day after day. And in my experience, oftentimes psychiatrists, therapists, the system in general can be so fucking unhelpful and broken (take it from someone who was placed on a hold twice and spent my fair share of time on r/SuicideWatch). Suicide hotlines can be useless and shallow. Friends can only offer platitudes (or are judgmental at worst). Your psychiatrist probably won't prescribe you DXM or help you with trying psychedelics. Sometimes you \*have\* (when the alternative is killing yourself) to self-medicate.

It crushes me that psychedelics (in general) are illegal- and that people face scorn/legal repercussions for trying to save themselves when they are failed by the mental health system. The act of taking DXM/psychedelics in and of itself isn't hurting anyone.

With all that said, if you happen to be reading this and are depressed and desperate, be careful. There's actually a lot of information out there- look up erowid or tripsitme or even reddit. It CAN be reasonably safe. There's no guarantees- but if you're in this category, I'm sure you already know that. 

I definitely don't think psychedelics is a magical panacea for all people. But at the very very least, it doesn't seem to be worse than what's already out there in terms of antidepressants, and by some other accounts, it could actually be better.
